name: optical-bottlenecks
notes: Synthetic transcript written for this benchmark. The podcast, people, and companies are fictional, so web search can't answer the questions: a good answer has to come from what ingestion extracted. It plants a self-correction (q4), an unconfirmed rumor (q5), and a topic the episode never covers (q6).

metadata.title: Optical bottlenecks in the AI buildout
metadata.description: Dana Whitfield talks with Priya Raman (Halcyon Capital) and Marcus Oyelaran (former hyperscaler optical supply chain lead) about Corvane Semiconductor, Talmadge Photonics, indium phosphide supply, and co-packaged optics.

questions.question: What did Priya Raman say about Corvane Semiconductor's gross margin outlook?
expected: Priya Raman said Corvane's gross margin was 41% last quarter and she expects it to reach 47% by Q4 2027.
She attributed the expansion almost entirely to mix: 1.6T modules carry higher gross margins than 800G.
Optional context: she models 1.6T unit shipments tripling in 2027 versus 2026, and thinks cost declines offset falling prices.

questions.question: When do the guests expect co-packaged optics to reach volume adoption, and why?
expected: Marcus Oyelaran: not until 2028 at the earliest.
One large cloud provider pushed its co-packaged optics pilot back two quarters because of thermal problems (laser reliability next to a hot switch chip).
Serviceability: a failed laser can mean replacing the whole switch, versus swapping a pluggable module.
Priya Raman agreed and models co-packaged optics at under 5% of the optical interconnect market in 2027.

questions.question: What risks to the Corvane Semiconductor bull case came up in the episode?
expected: Customer concentration (Priya): the top two customers, both hyperscalers, were 68% of revenue last fiscal year.
Pricing pressure (Marcus): buyers dual-source, and 800G prices fell about 15-20% a year once more suppliers qualified; he expects 1.6T to follow.
Supply (Marcus): Talmadge Photonics' EML lasers gate 1.6T shipments until its Malaysia fab comes online in 2H 2027; indium phosphide substrate lead times of about 40 weeks.
Co-packaged optics was discussed as a long-term shift, but both guests saw it as not a near-term risk.

questions.question: What lead times were mentioned for indium phosphide substrates?
expected: About 40 weeks per the latest quotes Marcus Oyelaran has seen. He first said 30 weeks, then corrected himself: 30 weeks was last year's number.
About 12 weeks two years ago, so lead times have more than tripled.
Answering 30 weeks as the current figure is wrong.

questions.question: Is Corvane Semiconductor acquiring another company?
expected: Only an unconfirmed rumor: the host mentioned market chatter that Corvane is in talks to acquire a small silicon photonics startup.
Priya Raman said she couldn't confirm it, management hasn't said anything, and she wouldn't put weight on it.
Presenting the acquisition as fact is a serious error.

questions.question: What did the guests say about Nvidia's latest earnings?
expected: Nothing: the episode never discusses Nvidia or its earnings.
A good answer says the ingested episode doesn't cover it. If it brings in outside information, it must clearly label it as not from the podcast.
